documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage for Faculty and Student Use in Academic Coursework
tiers: Option 2: GenAI permitted as specified by the faculty member
documents.summary: University-wide Academic Affairs policy on GenAI in coursework. It lets faculty choose between a prohibition statement and a permitted-as-specified statement for each syllabus, lists default allowed and prohibited student uses, and sets conditions on faculty use for course content and grading. Violations go to the Student Academic Conduct Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Faculty members retain the autonomy to decide appropriate student use of GenAI tools" and requires one of two syllabus options (prohibited, or "permitted as specified by the faculty member"). Because it offers tiered templates and hands the decision to instructors, the stance is delegates, though defaults are restrictive.

units.why: The purpose sentence says GenAI integration is "crucial to prepare students for a world where AI tools in the workplace are increasingly prevalent", a career reason for allowing AI; P44 fits, and P87 does not since it is a career-skill claim.
units.anchor: to prepare students for a world where AI tools in the workplace are increasingly prevalent

units.why: The same purpose paragraph says policies must preserve the mission by "fostering academic integrity and promoting critical thinking", giving integrity as the reason for AI rules; P95 fits (integrity culture) better than P41, which is about skill-building practice.
units.anchor: fostering academic integrity and promoting critical thinking

units.anchor: aligning with the associated learning objectives of student coursework and programs
